Description: At dawn, another corpse appears inside Victoria Maseko’s room even though the door was locked from the inside all night. After breaking in, everyone confirms an unexplained entry, and upon finding a pocket watch and hearing a gunshot, they quickly split up to act.
Location: Victoria Maseko’s room (Victoria's room)
Key Information:
  - At dawn, several people gather outside Victoria Maseko’s door and knock, confirming the door is locked from the inside.
  - Victoria Maseko says she found a corpse in the room the moment she woke up and insists she did not open the door during the night.
  - After the door is opened, everyone confirms a new corpse has appeared in the room, with no explainable way it could have entered.
  - Based on the earlier node where Nos. 7 and 8 fell asleep together, the corpse can be inferred to be Person No. 8.
  - John Hobbes points out the corpse has a sturdy build and would be difficult to move, deepening the locked-room mystery.
  - A pocket watch is found in the room, echoing the earlier Dauer-family pocket watch disappearance.
  - Tony Dauer confirms the pocket watch is the one he mentioned and questions how it could have entered a locked room.
  - Tony Dauer says he was previously in the Attic with Annie Beaumont.
  - Victoria Maseko says she saw something abnormal related to this the previous night but cannot fully explain it.
  - A sudden gunshot is heard, and Tony Dauer realizes the sound came from his police revolver.
  - Tony Dauer says his gun disappeared last night and that he locked his door, closely mirroring the current locked-room situation.
  - John Hobbes immediately asks whether anyone is missing from the group.
  - Annie Beaumont notes that Edmund Galley (No. 6) and Oswald (No. 3) are not present.
  - John Hobbes, Annie Beaumont, and Tony Dauer decide to immediately go look for the two missing people.
  - Martha Galley takes the emotionally unstable Victoria Maseko to the Dining room for breakfast, trying to stabilize the situation for the moment.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Is the first to recognize the irrationality of a corpse appearing in a locked room.
    · Notices the corpse’s build and emphasizes the difficulty of moving it.
    · Quickly organizes people after the gunshot and asks who is missing.
    · Decides to search for the absent people together with Annie Beaumont and Tony Dauer.
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie Beaumont)] Person No. 2.
    · Arrives at Victoria Maseko’s room to check the situation.
    · Points out that Edmund Galley and Oswald are not present.
    · Acts together with John Hobbes and Tony Dauer.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son.
    · Confirms the pocket watch found in the room belongs to the Dauer family.
    · Realizes the gunshot came from his revolver.
    · Says his gun went missing overnight even though his door was locked.
    · Joins the search for the missing people.
  [Martha Galley (Martha Galley)] Person No. 5, the female host of the villa.
    · Soothes Victoria Maseko emotionally.
    · Takes Victoria Maseko to the Dining room for breakfast to temporarily avoid the scene.
  [Victoria Maseko (Victoria)] Person No. 7.
    · Finds a newly appeared corpse inside a locked room at dawn.
    · Insists she did not open the door during the night.
    · Is visibly shaken and needs others to calm her.
